import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_93/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_93/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on Mouse ID
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Mouse ID", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema: ['Drug', 'Timepoint', 'Mouse ID']
# Convert Mouse ID to integer if possible (target schema says integer)
# But source Mouse ID is string, target Mouse ID is integer - so convert Mouse ID to integer if possible
# Check if Mouse ID values are numeric strings, else map them to integers by some method
# From examples, Mouse ID in source is string like 'n763', 'q787', 'y163' but target Mouse ID is integer like 25, 24
# So we need to convert Mouse ID strings to integers by extracting digits only

# Extract digits from Mouse ID string to convert to integer
joined["Mouse ID"] = joined["Mouse ID"].str.extract("(\d+)").astype(int)

# Reorder columns
result = joined[["Drug", "Timepoint", "Mouse ID"]]

# Group by Drug (primary key) to ensure uniqueness (FD: Drug -> Mouse ID)
# Since FD says Drug determines Mouse ID, group by Drug and take first Mouse ID and first Timepoint
result = result.groupby("Drug", as_index=False).agg({
    "Timepoint": "first",
    "Mouse ID": "first"
})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_93/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
